title: Revision-aware Ephemeral Handoff Controller with Rollback Scribe
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a revision-aware ephemeral handoff controller that records a compact rollback scribe for deterministic revert and replay; adds supporting telemetry and a runbook. Backward compatible with existing rollout policies.
description: Context & motivation: We need a safer way to perform short-lived handoffs between model revisions during canary/AB workflows and shadow-to-active promotions where session affinity and transient state can complicate rollback. Current promote/drain paths can lose causal information required to deterministically revert or replay traffic for forensics. This PR implements an ephemeral handoff controller that attaches a minimal "scribe" (compacted event sketch) to promotions; the scribe captures revision boundaries, cohort assignment, and key telemetry anchors to drive deterministic rollback and accelerated replay.

review_comments: Claire Ng: Great overall design. Two questions: 1) How does the scribe size behave under high QPS? 2) Are there any privacy/PII risks when recording cohort keys?

Author (Asha): Scribe is a compact sketch (HyperLogLog-like summary) limited to 1KB by default; full payloads are not captured. Cohort keys are hashed and salted per-customer; docs updated with privacy notes.
Diego Morales: Request change - add a circuit-breaker that stops scribe emission if latency impacted (seen in perf smoke).
Author (Asha): Added backpressure + rate-limiter to scribe emitter (new commit 3c9a1f2) and perf tests. See integration test for latency guard.
Samir Kapoor: Minor nit - helm flag naming inconsistent with other controllers. Suggest rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled -> rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled (kept for parity).
Author (Asha): Kept the flag to match existing convention; added comment in values.yaml to clarify.
Claire Ng: Approved after code changes and documentation updates. Diego approved on second pass.
ci_checks: integration-tests: initial failure on latent race; rerun passed
perf-smoke: warn (0.3% p99 increase under synthetic load) - mitigated by scribe backpressure
merge: Merged by squash via main at 2026-02-22 after approvals. Merge commit includes summarized changelog and runbook link.
testing_and_validation: Unit + integration coverage added for state transitions and deterministic revert; synthetic e2e validated canary->promote->replay path with session-affine traffic and verified fidelity within 0.4% of baseline. Load test included 10K RPS ephemeral handoffs with scribe rate-limited and no user-visible latency regression after backpressure enabled.
rollout_plan: Feature is behind helm flag rollout.ephemeralHandoff.enabled=false by default. Initial rollout: enable on non-prod clusters for 48h, enable on a small cohort (1% traffic) in staging for 24h with smoke checks, then enable for selective customers under dedicated capacity. If metrics breach: auto-backout policy triggers (see runbook) and scribe provides deterministic replay to reproduce issue.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: rollout.scribe.emitted_count, rollout.scribe.overlimit, rollout.handoff.latency_p99. Alerts added: ScribeErrorRate > 0.1% for 5m, HandoffLatencyP99 > 200ms for 3m. Dashboards added to Console rollout detail + service-level tracing linked.
migration_notes: No DB schema migrations. Controller persists lightweight markers in existing rollout ledger; it is backward compatible with older controllers (they will ignore scribe blobs). Operators should ensure helm values are synchronized across clusters before enabling.
docs: Added docs/runbooks/rollback-scribe.md with operator playbook, example curl commands to download scribe artifacts, and forensic replay steps. Console changes expose a 'Download scribe' button on rollout details.
related_prs_and_work_items: Related Linear: ENG-1982 (handoff telemetry design), ENG-2030 (runbook & operator training). References: RFC 'handoff-scribe-2026' and prior incident notes in INT-4512.
security_and_privacy: Scribe payloads are compact, hashed, and stored with customer scoping. Added KMS encryption at rest for scribe artifacts when stored beyond retention window. Privacy review completed and documented in docs/privacy/rollout-telemetry.md.
operational_playbook_snippet: If a promotion causes regression: 1) Use Console to 'Pause rollout' (holdpoint). 2) Download scribe and run replay tool (scripts/replay/replay_from_scribe.py) in dry-run mode. 3) If replay reproduces issue, execute 'rollback via scribe' which replays traffic against previous revision and automates swap. Follow runbook steps to notify customer success for affected cohorts.
notes: This PR aims to improve determinism for fast promotes and automated rollbacks. It does not change existing routing or session affinity semantics. Future work: expose scribe-based automated bisect tooling and long-term archival options.
changelog: Added EphemeralHandoffController, scribe serializer/emitter, Console visualization, helm toggle, integration tests, and operator runbook.
